verdict: Scoped review passes with explicit remaining source namespace and bounded completeness limits.
review_scope: Read-only independent review of final purchase-summary repacking and ProductGroup shared-child ordering. This receipt does not replace the full 603-case benchmark or the separate all-corpus raw record audit.

fixed_finding.description: Before the strict guard, an otherwise matching Purchase option summary carrying a conflict flag, field mapping, or its own source pointer could be removed. Such metadata made the summary unique evidence even when its display text had an exact typed proof.
fixed_finding.synthetic_reproduction: 125 unique higher-priority facts, one complete typed variant, one matching summary with unique metadata, and a two-chunk media object under the 128-fact bound.
fixed_finding.resolution: The implementing agent added a strict allowed-key test: only label, value, source_type, source_url and supporting_sources are eligible. Conflict, field, source_path, part, section, source_locator and any future preserved metadata block removal.
fixed_finding.limitation: The defect was demonstrated with synthetic inputs; this review does not claim an affected member record or an observed production incident.

code_review_findings.result: Only an existing unstructured Purchase option summary containing exactly the allowed display/source keys can be removed by the completion pass. Facts carrying unique conflict/field/pointer/part/section/form metadata survive this pass.

A complete retained JSON record or complete exact-property projection must reproduce the summary label and value. The proof must exist at a variants index and preserve the summary-generating properties. Numeric minor-unit price wording and explicit weight-unit wording are not treated as equivalent to different string prices or units.

Each primary and supporting URL/source-type pair requires its own proof. An unrelated query URL, source type, or form cannot lend proof. Source URL, selected form locator and exact pointer remain part of JSON group identity.

A proposed restored JSON group must have contiguous part indices starting at zero and parse as complete JSON. A missing first chunk, a gap, malformed JSON, or chunks from different URL/form namespaces do not justify removing a summary.

The completion pass restores a partial retained JSON group, a selected top-level image/media object, or an omitted direct child of a retained projection. It does not unconditionally promote wholly omitted new variant cores.

Completion removes only the proven redundant summaries; the independent pressure cases preserve every unique higher-priority filler. Separately, exact ProductGroup child/reference priority now precedes page projections so a needed shared child survives earlier page-only merges. This ordering still operates within existing bounds and does not guarantee all lower-priority captions or records fit.

The unchanged limits remain 128 facts, 64000 aggregate label/value/section/pointer/form characters, and 1600 characters per value. Replacement checks both aggregate count and character capacity before mutation. Source attribution metadata retains its pre-existing separate bound.

Any omission already sets truncation and completion never clears it. Fitting records remain unflagged. Under unavoidable character or fact pressure, incomplete JSON fragments can remain with the global truncation flag; this is not a claim that every exported record is complete.

Both Larry pages publish two ProductGroup objects whose first variants use the same relative hasVariant pointer. The output preserves exact alternatives but lacks a JSON-LD script/object locator. The two alternatives must remain distinct in the audit; a single unambiguous object at that URL/path cannot be claimed.

limitations: This detects and source-checks mixed-format paths in the supplied focused replay only; it is not an all-corpus ambiguity census.
Current facts lack a JSON-LD script/object locator. Exact alternatives can be source-reviewed, but their shared URL/path is not a unique object namespace.
Successful source reconstruction does not establish unverified preview values as canonical or erase source_facts_truncated.

object_hash_encoding: SHA256 of UTF-8 JSON with keys sorted, ensure_ascii=false, comma/colon separators and no final newline. Source file hashes are SHA256 of original bytes.
final_limits: The 27 controls are focused synthetic checks, not an independent benchmark corpus.
The actual namespace scan covers all 17 cases in the stable focused replay, not an all-603 namespace census.
Exact reconstruction of each Larry alternative is supported by original captured bytes. It does not remove the mixed namespace or justify silently merging their different fields.
No frozen expected result was changed, and no post-output source review was used to increase a frozen benchmark score.
No canonical coffee field, Pending/Verified decision, member data, offline code, external application or deployment was changed by this review.
